question.text: While reviewing a fresh AIF registration application, SEBI examines the 'fit and proper' criteria for the Sponsor and Manager as defined under Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008. Which of the following is NOT part of that criteria?

answer.text: No history of restraint orders and convictions
Financial competence based on net worth and solvency
Minimum INR 10 crore paid-up capital of the Sponsor entity

explanation.text: The Logic: Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 (as referenced in Reg 4 of AIF Regulations) defines 'fit and proper' on four parameters: (i) integrity, reputation and character; (ii) no history of restraint orders/convictions; (iii) financial competence based on net worth and solvency; (iv) no history of being a wilful defaulter. There is no specific minimum paid-up capital requirement for Sponsor. The Trap: Option D sounds plausible (capital adequacy is familiar from banking/NBFC registration) but is not part of AIF fit-and-proper. The AIF regime uses the 'continuing interest' sponsor-commit rule (Reg 10) rather than a paid-up-capital floor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests fit-and-proper identically. III-A Compliance exam covers Schedule II in depth. Broker/intermediary exams use the same standard. Cat III Managers (XIX-E future) apply same criteria. Manager's Pro-Tip: When structuring first-time AIF Managers, document (a) CA/CS/auditor certificates of net worth, (b) CIBIL/defaulter-check reports for key personnel, (c) character references from prior employers and (d) declarations of no pending litigation. SEBI RTA returns applications frequently for missing declarations.
